thread:
sara: Quick q — we just upgraded openssl in runtime image. No public API change, no behavior change we can find. Do we treat this as a patch bump or something else?
kevin: semver wise: deps-only, backward-compatible bugfix -> patch. If it could change runtime behavior for some edge cases, might need a minor with a note.
raj: Agree patch for consumers. Ops note: some customers pin at minor not patch, so changelog visibility matters.
lena: tagging conv? do we keep tags plain `v1.2.4` or add a buildmeta `v1.2.4+openssl-1.1.2`?
kevin: prefer plain `v1.2.4` and put build details in the changelog/release notes. Avoid changing tag semantics.
sara: ok. And release notes: short bullet 'runtime: openssl upgrade (CVE fixed), no API change)'. Good?
alicia: add rollback criteria to the deploy: canary error-rate > 0.8% OR tail latency p95 > 3x baseline in first 15m -> rollback. Also log size spike check.
raj: +1 on rollback thresholds. Could we have deploy-bot enforce canary window and auto-rollback?
deploy-bot: deploy started: service=runtime-image environment=prod canary=10% rollout=5m monitor=[errors,latency,logs]
lena: if deploy-bot can auto-rollback, we should include a manual override for infra folks. e.g. `deploy undo --force`
kevin: tagging command we'll use for this release: `git tag -a v1.2.4 -m "deps: openssl upgrade" && git push origin v1.2.4`
sara: can someone add a short line in RELEASE_NOTES.md and include the CVE link? I'll cut the release.
raj: I'll draft the release note and include customer note re: pinning behavior.
alicia: after canary looks good, bump to 100% rollout and mark as shipped in JIRA. Otherwise rollback and create hotfix branch.
sara: decision: bump patch to v1.2.4, tag plain `v1.2.4`, changelog with dep details, deploy with bot canary + thresholds above, auto-rollback enabled but manual override available. :thumbsup:
kevin: I'll publish the tag and kick off the deploy in 10m.
lena: I'll add the deploy-bot override instruction to the on-call runbook.
deploy-bot: canary healthy at 10% after 5m — errors normal, latency within baseline.
sara: thanks all, will follow up if rollback needed."
